issue_paraphrase: Test suites that declare several nested test classes inside the same enclosing test class are executed in an order taken straight from the JVM's reflection API, which is unspecified and differs between JDK versions and between machines. The same suite can therefore run its nested classes in different orders on different Java versions, which makes output-based comparisons and any order-sensitive test logic non-deterministic. The framework now orders nested classes declared in the same enclosing type using a deterministic (intentionally non-obvious) ordering algorithm.
fix_summary: ReflectionUtils.findNestedClasses (and ReflectionSupport wrappers) now sort classes returned by getDeclaredClasses() with a new defaultClassSorter that compares Class.getName().hashCode() first and falls back to lexicographic comparison on hashCode collision, applied through the existing toSortedMutableList helper. Result: same-enclosing-class nested classes always come out in the same deterministic order regardless of JVM. Javadoc updated to state the deterministic-but-nonobvious ordering contract.
notes: Only the full class-level --tests filter worked for JUnit Platform tests under Gradle 9.0.0 (the 'Class.methodName' form matches nothing: 'No tests found for given includes'); the class-level filter is fine because at the parent exactly one method of the 121 in the class fails. No network needed at test runtime. First Gradle run per working tree downloads the 9.0.0 distribution and Maven deps (~3 min); test task afterwards is seconds. The other test in the same class (findNestedClassesWithInvalidNestedClassFile) needs groovy on the classpath, which the module already declares, so it runs fine.

issue_paraphrase: Parameters passed to a parameterized test through CSV data sources have their leading and trailing whitespace trimmed by default. After a change in the whitespace handling, that trimming started using Unicode-aware whitespace detection, so non-ASCII whitespace such as non-breaking spaces was silently removed from argument values, and some other control characters were no longer trimmed at all. The values a test actually receives therefore changed between releases without any code change in the test, silently altering or breaking suites. Trimming should only apply to ASCII whitespace, matching the original behavior.
fix_summary: CsvReaderFactory's field-trimming line for unquoted CSV columns was changed from field.strip() (Unicode whitespace) back to field.trim() (ASCII controls/spaces <= U+0020), restoring pre-5.8-compatible trimming semantics. Javadoc on CsvSource.ignoreLeadingAndTrailingWhitespaces and CsvFileSource.ignoreLeadingAndTrailingWhitespaces documents that 'whitespace' means code points <= U+0020 as defined by String.trim().
notes: Class-level --tests filter used (method-name filter matches nothing under JUnit Platform + Gradle 8.14). Whole CsvArgumentsProviderTests class is green except the regression test at parent. No network at test runtime; build-time network only (wrapper + Maven deps). First run downloads gradle 8.14.2 and compiles jupiter-tests dependency graph (~3 min); subsequent runs seconds. Also note the referenced upstream context: junit-team/junit-framework#3824 comment, indicating users hit this as a silent behavior change after upgrading.

issue_paraphrase: When a superclass declared in a different package defines a test method, and a subclass declares a method with the same name and parameter list, the framework treats the inherited package-private method as overridden even though Java visibility rules mean it is not an override. As a result, the superclass's package-private test method is silently skipped, and only the subclass's method is discovered and executed. Tests that used to run therefore disappear from the results without any error or warning as soon as a subclass adds a method with the same signature.
fix_summary: Method selection was reworked so that a discovered method is always reported against the class that actually declares it. ClassSelectorResolver.selectMethod now builds a new DeclaredMethodSelector carrying the full list of candidate classes; MethodSelectorResolver/MethodSegmentResolver use it to resolve the declaring class via ReflectionUtils.findDeclaredMethods instead of the deleted MethodFinder heuristic (which decomposed the method segment and picked a single class). MethodSelector grew constructor/logic support for this. Net effect: a package-private superclass method in another package plus an unrelated same-signature subclass method are now both discovered and executed (with the same display name).
notes: Both golden tests are integration-style (JUnit Platform launcher + testkit) but completely offline. Class-level --tests filter used. First run per tree downloads gradle 9.2.0 and builds the jupiter-tests dependency graph (~3 min); subsequent runs seconds. The two displayed statistic assertions make this a robust oracle. The commit message references PR #5100 but the underlying issue it fixes is #5098.
